description: TX3 federal tax and customs statutes and regulations, admitted from the prepared source inventory; one instrument held out for the same structural parsing difficulty as lcmopfih.
notes: Normalized from prompts/cluster-2-batches/lex-mex-cl2-batch-TX3.json for the repository Rust ingestion gate.
All three prepared entries were absent from adapters, corpus/mx, and existing operational batch manifests when this manifest was created.

The prepared manifest's dof_publication/dof_last_reform fields are provenance context, not part of the operational batch-manifest schema, and are dropped here rather than smuggled in as unknown properties.
A live recheck of all three source_pdf URLs on 2026-08-01 returned HTTP 200 for each.

lisipl is held out per the ingestion-difficulty-log.md hold-out-and-flag policy (nested-law-in-enacting-article, second instance after TX2's lcmopfih): its source PDF's real content is enacted verbatim inside ARTICULO NOVENO of an unrelated 1968 instrument that is itself formally titled and enacted as a Ley despite being materially a reform decree, with that instrument's other articles elided. Simpler than lcmopfih: no dual-transitorios ambiguity, since the nested tax has no closing transitorios of its own and the document's single TRANSITORIOS section belongs unambiguously to the outer instrument. See docs/ingestion-difficulty-log.md for the full report.
Instrument order is preserved from the prepared cluster-2 plan.
